device.name: mrw-code morphology microscopy stage (v2 control window)

facts.text: README.md names v2_robot as the final version and robot/ as legacy code kept for completeness.
portConnection sets the pyserial port and baudrate from the GUI fields and opens the port.
Closing the port through portConnection clears portConnectStatus and sets systemCalibrate to False.
The control window sets the relative-move speed string to 'F50\n'.
The manual step-size spin box is bounded by setMinimum(0.0) and setMaximum(100.0).
A manual relative move writes '$J=G21G91' plus the axis, the spin box's textFromValue of the step value divided by 100.0 and speed_rel to the serial port, then sleeps 0.1 s.
Calibration writes '$X\n' and 'G10 P0 L20 X0 Y0 Z0\n' to an open serial port and sets the systemCalibrate software flag.
HOME writes 'G90 G0 X0 Y0\n' only when the port is open and systemCalibrate is true; it does not home Z.
getMonitorSystemValues only prints '@GETALLPOS' to stdout; it writes nothing to the port and reads no reply.
quitSystem calls explorationThread.stop(), closes the serial port and closes the window; it writes no command to the controller.
The exploration stop() sets ThreadActive to false, joins the subscriber thread with timeout 0 and calls quit(); it writes nothing to the serial port.
The exploration run loop busy-waits in 'while config.pictureSaved == False' and 'while not self.shall_i_move' without checking ThreadActive.
After its row loops the exploration run writes 'G90 G0 X0 Y0' to the port.
The v2 ROS subscriber calls rospy.Subscriber on the relative name do_inference_topic (String) and rospy.Publisher on the relative name ready_move (Bool), then rospy.spin().
QtCapture creates a publisher on the relative topic do_inference_topic, initialises the anonymous ROS node inference_trigger and opens the camera with cv2.VideoCapture(0).
The exploration thread subscribes to the relative topic ready_move; its callback stores the Boolean in shall_i_move.
The ControlWindow constructor prints every serial port device it lists.

determinism.notes: State-machine fake with placeholder positions and replies; no Qt event loop, serial port, camera, G-code interpreter or ROS graph runs

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS-free Python stand-in for the PyQt control window
gaps: the fake records G-code writes and updates placeholder GUI/axis state; it does not execute G-code, step a motor, capture an image or publish on ROS
the upstream serial protocol is one-way in this path: there is no position, completion or stop acknowledgement to model
the camera/JPG capture path and the do_inference_topic/ready_move handshake are not exposed

no acknowledged stop: quitSystem writes no command to the controller, so the e-stop reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED; an exploration run that is busy-waiting for a picture or for ready_move does not see the stop flag, and its final home write fails only because the port is closed

the real device is an Arduino G-code stage, not a simulator; the card's simulated mode comes from the registry record, and the upstream window needs a Qt display, prints to stdout (a risk for an MHS server on stdio) and must be calibrated again after the port is reopened

the fake formats the divided step with %g; the upstream uses QDoubleSpinBox.textFromValue, whose decimals and locale (Qt, outside the clone; the clone sets no decimals) can round the value, so the exact G-code strings in the tests are fake-only

safe_state.description: No acknowledged stop exists: the e-stop runs the upstream Exit path (exploration thread stopped, serial port and window closed) and reports MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held. Nothing is sent to the G-code controller, so moves it has already received may continue; nothing confirms that the stage stopped.
